title: Inverse image along an isomorphism of schemes on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $g^{-1}$, $g_*$ and the structure maps $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ be the inverse image, direct image and structure maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then:

1. The functor $\Phi_g:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\mapsto(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$, is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse $(V\xrightarrow{v}Y)\mapsto(V\xrightarrow{g^{-1}\circ v}X)$; both functors send coverings to coverings. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ there is an isomorphism $(g^{-1}\mathcal F)(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\cong\mathcal F(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$, natural in $\mathcal F$ and in $U$.
2. $g^{-1}$ is an equivalence of categories from sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (of sets, abelian groups, rings, or modules over a constant sheaf of rings), with quasi-inverse $g_*$. In particular $g^{-1}$ is exact and commutes with all small limits and colimits; for every inverse system $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq1}$ of sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the canonical map $g^{-1}\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n\to\varprojlim_ng^{-1}\mathcal F_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], induced by the inverse images of the projections, is an isomorphism.
3. For every commutative ring $A$ the structure map $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings, and for every ring homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, with $\varphi_Y:A_Y\to B_Y$ and $\varphi_X:A_X\to B_X$ the induced maps of constant sheaves, $\varphi_X\circ c^g_A=c^g_B\circ g^{-1}(\varphi_Y)$.

proof.text: Write $h$ for the inverse scheme isomorphism. By [lem-weil-iso-weakly-etale], both $g$ and $h$ are weakly etale. Weakly etale composition makes $\Phi_g(U,u)=(U,gu)$ and $\Phi_h(V,v)=(V,hv)$ functors on the recorded small sites. The equations $hg=1_X$ and $gh=1_Y$ identify their composites with the identity on objects and arrows, with the canonical representative isomorphisms if small skeletons are used. A covering is specified by its underlying scheme arrows and their fpqc covering condition, which postcomposition does not change. Thus both functors preserve and reflect coverings.

proof.text: Fix $(U,u)$ and write $U_Y=(U,gu)$. In the indexing category $\mathcal I_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the object $D_U=(U_Y,\theta_U)$ with $\theta_U=(u,1_U):U\to X\times_YU_Y$ is initial. Indeed the unique arrow $D_U\to(V,\phi)$ is $a=\operatorname{pr}_2\phi:U_Y\to V$: the equation $u_g(a)\theta_U=\phi$ follows from the two fibre-product projections, and that equation forces $a=\operatorname{pr}_2\phi$. Consequently $D_U$ is terminal in $\mathcal I_U^{op}$. The colimit cocone with vertex $\mathcal F(U_Y)$ has maps restriction along these $a$. Its inverse is the colimit coprojection at $D_U$; the cocone equations make both composites identities. For $b:U^\prime\to U$, the same formula gives restriction along $b_Y$; for a sheaf morphism it gives its component at $U_Y$. This proves naturality in both variables, including for abelian groups and rings because all maps used are their restriction homomorphisms. This is the elementary terminal-object colimit argument (Mathlib also states it as colimitOfDiagramTerminal).

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites] to the equivalence in Step 1. Its full-faithfulness, quasi-inverse and covering-iff hypotheses were verified there; the sites are small in the universe fixed by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Hence $T\mathcal F(U)=\mathcal F(U_Y)$ and $S\mathcal G(V)=\mathcal G(V_X)$ are inverse equivalences on set and abelian sheaves, where $V_X=(V,hv)$. For ring sheaves, the same functors use the operations already present at $U_Y$ or $V_X$; the unit and counit identities respect every operation. Thus they also give inverse equivalences on ring sheaves. Step 2 identifies the inverse-image presheaf with $T\mathcal F$, already a sheaf, so its sheafification is itself by its universal property. This proves the section formula for the specified $g^{-1}$, rather than merely constructing an abstract equivalence. Sectionwise implementation (IsoSectionwiseInverseImage): use the already stated proEtaleIsoPostcompose_equivalence for the two covering-preserving functors. Mathlib Functor.isContinuous_iff_coverPreserving supplies continuity because an equivalence is representably flat. Construct the sheaf equivalence explicitly with sheafPushforwardContinuousComp and sheafPushforwardContinuousId', allowing independent coefficient object and Hom universes. This directly proves isoSectionwiseInverseImage_equivalence, including arbitrary-size limit and colimit preservation by equivalence.

proof.text: The isomorphism $X\times_YV\cong V_X$ over $X$ has forward map $\operatorname{pr}_2$ and inverse $(hv,1_V)$. Restriction along it identifies the specified $g_*\mathcal G(V)=\mathcal G(X\times_YV)$ with $S\mathcal G(V)$, naturally in $V,\mathcal G$. Combined with $g^{-1}\cong T$ from Step 3, this proves the asserted quasi-inverse is $g_*$. The equivalences preserve every existing small limit and colimit by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits]. On abelian sheaves they are additive (addition of maps is unchanged sectionwise); kernels and cokernels are the finite limit and colimit constructions, so the equivalence is exact.

Let $P_Y,P_X$ be the constant ring presheaves with value $A$. To apply [lem-pc-dense-subsite-sheafification-compatibility] to $\Phi_g$, note that it is fully faithful, every target object is isomorphic to one in its image and hence covered by one, and its topology is induced because it preserves and reflects coverings. Restriction is the ring-sheaf equivalence of Step 3, and ring sheafification exists as in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Since $T(P_Y)=P_X$, the compatibility theorem identifies $T(A_Y)$ with $A_X$. Choose the unique isomorphism $\beta_A:T(A_Y)\to A_X$ whose composite with $P_X\to T(A_Y)$ is the constant-presheaf sheafification unit; uniqueness of sheafification gives this normalization. In particular it sends the image of each constant $a$ to the image of the same $a$. Sectionwise implementation: the inverse site functor preserves covers, so Adjunction.isCocontinuous_iff_coverPreserving makes Phi_g cocontinuous. Its Mathlib pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility, evaluated at the constant commutative-ring presheaf, gives the required isomorphism. The lemma toSheafify_pullbackSheafificationCompatibility proves its normalization on constant sections. The fully faithful functor forgetting commutativity transports this to ring sheaves. For uniqueness lift a ring-sheaf morphism through that fully faithful functor, cancel the comparison inverse, and apply sheafify_hom_ext; this proves isoSectionwiseConstantMap_existsUnique without the dense-subsite lemma.

source.place: Tags 00WH and 0H7J; compatibility is the cited Mathlib leaf at DenseSubsite/Basic.lean:805

proof.text: Under Step 2, the candidate $\beta_A\circ(g^{-1}A_Y\cong T(A_Y))$ has adjoint $A_Y\to g_*A_X$ which sends every constant $a$ over $V$ to its constant section over $X\times_YV$. Indeed the adjunction unit, the composite of the $u_p\dashv u^p$ and sheafification adjunctions in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], is the coprojection indexed by $(V,1)$ followed by the sheafification unit, and Step 2 sends it to restriction along $\operatorname{pr}_2:(X\times_YV)_Y\to V$. By sheafification uniqueness this adjoint equals the map $\rho^g_A$ defining $c^g_A$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Therefore $c^g_A$ is the displayed isomorphism. If $\varphi:A\to B$, the two composites $\varphi_Xc^g_A$ and $c^g_Bg^{-1}(\varphi_Y)$, viewed on $T(A_Y)$, both send each constant $a$ to the constant $\varphi(a)$. The sheafification universal property makes them equal. This proves exactly the prescribed naturality equation. Sectionwise implementation: the uniqueness just proved identifies the chosen isoSectionwiseConstantMap with the image under forgetful sheaf composition of the comparison isomorphism. Functors preserve isomorphisms, proving isoSectionwiseConstantMap_isIso. The original module continues to state the comparison with the recorded inverse-image construction and coefficient naturality.

proof.text: For an $A_Y$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$, sectionwise precomposition $T$ gives a $T(A_Y)$-module sheaf: the action and every module identity at $U$ are those at $U_Y$, and restrictions are the original semilinear maps. Apply [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] with $R=T(A_Y)$, $S=A_X$, $c=\beta_A$ and $M=T\mathcal F$. Its normalized tensor isomorphism identifies the actual scalar-extended module pullback of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] with $T\mathcal F$ carrying action $b\cdot x=\beta_{A,U}^{-1}(b)x$. Thus the tensor comparison previously proved inline is now the statement of a cited general lemma.

source.place: Tags 03CZ and 03EK; general ring-isomorphism tensor comparison specialized to beta_A

proof.text: For an $A_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal G$, give $S\mathcal G$ its $A_Y$-action through $S(\beta_A):A_Y\cong S(A_X)$ and $ST\cong1$. Step 4 identifies $S\mathcal G$ with $g_*\mathcal G$. The scalar map under this identification equals $\rho^g_A$: both sheaf ring maps $A_Y\to g_*A_X$ agree on the constant presheaf by Step 6, so agree by sheafification uniqueness. Thus this is the actual module direct image. The sectionwise unit and counit $ST\cong1$ and $TS\cong1$ are linear: their scalar identifications are $\beta_A$ and its inverse, whose composites are identities. Hence these are quasi-inverse module functors. They preserve addition on morphisms; by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] they preserve limits and colimits. The recorded module category is abelian, so preservation of kernels and cokernels proves exactness. Sectionwise implementation for arbitrary isomorphic coefficient sheaves: let phi = inv c and let psi be the sheaf-adjunction unit followed by the inverse site transport of c. The first compatibility is the unit formula and c followed by inv c equals identity. The second follows from naturality of the counit and the left triangle identity. Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence then identifies the existing isoSectionwiseModuleInverseImage definition with the equivalence functor. Its map on every section is the original module homomorphism, so it preserves addition; equivalence supplies finite limits and colimits. This proves isoSectionwiseModuleInverseImage_exact directly for the sectionwise definition, without constructing tensor scalar extension.

Apply limit preservation to the tower $(\mathcal F_n)$. For modules, abelian groups and rings, [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] supplies its limit and coordinate projections. For sets the compatible-tuple presheaf is a sheaf: glue coordinatewise using the sheaf axioms of $\mathcal F_n$; transition equations hold because they hold locally and $\mathcal F_n$ is separated. The tuple of any cone maps is its unique map to this sheaf, proving its limit property. In each case [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] makes the image of the original limit cone a limit cone. The comparison with the chosen target limit has inverse given by the opposite universal property; the composites are identities because they agree with identities after every projection. Its projection composites are $g^{-1}$ of the original projections, so it is exactly the canonical map in the statement.
